questions.q: Which keyboard model ships for review — single letters, modifier keys, or single letters scoped to the drawer?
questions.lede: Three incompatible key maps for one act sit in the corpus, none is in the code, and single letters carry a level-A duty nobody costed.

cells: j / k, per the hint chip

rows.label: Third verb
cells: s, skip; absent from the hint

questions.stakes: `r` means reject in one map and revert in another, which are opposite acts on the same span.
state: The code types the world as `mod+k | mod+p | mod+g` (`src/modules/app-shell/presentation/use-hotkey.ts:5`) plus three authoring keys.
No review key exists, and there is no review-state code in `src/` at all.
The plan says one key reverts any span (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:20`) and never names the key.
path: Each research round designed a map against its own surface: a proposal render, then a located AI edit, then the review drawer.
The prototype then disagreed with itself. The drawer's buttons offer accept, revert and skip; its hint chip omits skip (`docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:458`).
tension: Single letters are the fast map and the one WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.4 flags at level A (`k4-accessibility.md:106`).
The recorded remedies are a remap screen, a modifier requirement, or restricting the keys to focus.
A remap screen is priced at 3-4 days for two founders (`r24-v1-table-stakes.md:36`) and no exhibit carries it.
A reader's caret usually sits in the document, not in the drawer, so focus scoping costs reach.

recCase: Focus scoping gives the speed of single letters and the compliance of modifiers for the price of one rule.

questions.q: Do the table-stakes interaction days go into MVP-0, and does Cmd-K move to insert-link with them?
questions.lede: The sequence spends 69 of about 70 engineering days before it reaches the line that reads table stakes and polish.

state: Six named blocks in the sequence sum to 69 days against a stated total of about 70 (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:227`).
The measured floor is eight items at 13-21 days, midpoint 17.5, and none of them is scheduled (`docs/CRITIQUE.md:602`).
`insertLink` is written and reachable only by mouse (`src/modules/editor/presentation/toolbar-transforms.ts:234`, `Toolbar.tsx:102`).
Cmd-K opens the note switcher (`src/modules/app-shell/presentation/KnowledgeUI.tsx:56`); the prototype's status bar says a third thing (`prototype:315`).
path: The editor shell came from sgnk-md, where 41 of 43 editor files are byte-identical. Nobody chose these bindings for this product.
The floor was measured by reading the code against the published key maps of Obsidian, Typora, Bear, iA Writer, Zed and VS Code.
tension: In Typora, Bear, iA Writer, Obsidian and VS Code, Cmd-K is insert-link (`docs/CRITIQUE.md:614`). Here it opens a file switcher.
r24-v1 prices the floor in days for two founders; the commit record is 80 of 80 by one author (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:231`).
At the measured 1.21 engineering days a calendar week, 17.5 more days is roughly fourteen more weeks.
A VS Code extension inherits the whole floor and the keymap from the host and deletes this decision (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:364`).

questions.q: Do we run the 40-hunk head-to-head against `git add -p` in weeks 1-2, before building the review surface?
questions.lede: The record holds a costed argument that the review interaction is theatre on any change big enough to need it, and a written falsifier.

visual.note: What survives the comparison is word grain, dirty buffers and the hash line.
visual.caption: The same 40 hunks, in the paid surface and the free one.

questions.stakes: Eighteen engineering days of review-state build rest on an interaction that may collapse to accept-all on any change large enough to matter.
state: Weeks 1-2 lists six items and the 40-hunk comparison is not among them (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:352`).
One of those six, the Obsidian plugin, is cut ten lines earlier (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:304`).
Review state is priced at 18 engineering days: store 6, rendering 5, revert 3, panel 4 (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:56`).
The falsifier is already written with thresholds (`docs/CRITIQUE.md:643`).
path: The comparison was made in the 2026-08-31 critique, against an earlier version of the interaction.
The plan has been rewritten four times since and the falsifier was never carried forward.
tension: Review to generation runs 17-25x on a 40-hunk change, and worsens as agents produce larger changes (`docs/CRITIQUE.md:637`).
Cisco measured no useful review above 250 lines and a 60-minute wear-out. That is source code, and the mapping onto markdown spans is an analogy.
Google measured a 3.2-hour weekly review budget against a 24-line median change.
What genuinely survives is narrow: word-grain hunks, hunks in a dirty buffer, and the hash line (`docs/CRITIQUE.md:641`).

state: F2 ships a review panel with a counter, and the tree carries unreviewed bars (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:56`).
The panel is designed as a persistent list rather than a per-session diff (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:383`).
The drawer headline counts unreviewed spans in this file, walked one at a time (`docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:458`).
Nothing in the plan caps how many spans are surfaced in one sitting.
path: The list is the affordance the category converged on: GitHub's file list, Zed's agent panel, the diff pane in four editors.
The attention evidence arrived afterwards and runs the other way.
tension: Cisco found no useful review above 250 lines and a 60-minute wear-out. That is source code, and the mapping onto markdown spans is an analogy.
Google measured a 3.2-hour weekly review budget against a 24-line median change.
The one clinical system that earned acceptance fired 31 rules in 0.19% of 500,274 sessions, at 57.5% acceptance.
Suppression means ranking, and a ranking is state the projection law says must be derivable from the file alone.

options.label: Suppression by default, with the full list one click away
options.what: The panel opens on a filtered set, and the rule is a deterministic function of the file.
gains: Matches every measured system that kept acceptance
Nothing is hidden, only deferred behind one click
costs: A rule that is wrong hides the thing that mattered
The rule has to be explainable in one sentence
options.system: The filter must be derivable from the bytes, or the projection law breaks.
options.screens: The panel gains a filtered default and a show-everything control.

options.label: Enumeration as today: every changed span, in document order
options.what: The panel lists everything and the person works down it.
gains: No rule to explain and nothing can be hidden
Matches what the category has converged on
costs: The list stops being read long before it ends
Every override measurement in the evidence is against it
options.system: No change.
options.screens: No change.

options.label: A budget rather than a filter: a fixed number of spans a sitting
options.what: The surface offers a capped batch and defers the rest to the next sitting.
gains: Respects the measured wear-out without ranking anything
No judgement about which span matters
costs: An arbitrary number nobody has measured for prose
Deferred spans still accumulate
options.system: A counter and a cut-off; no ranking state.
options.screens: The panel gains an end-of-batch state.

options.label: Enumeration, plus a dismissal rate that retires a span class
options.what: Show everything, and stop surfacing a class of change once it is ignored past a stated rate.
gains: The suppression is learned rather than guessed
Tricorder's probation threshold is a precedent
costs: Needs live counts before it does anything
The first weeks are pure enumeration
options.system: Per-class dismissal counts in the local usage file.
options.screens: No new screen; classes quietly stop appearing.

recCase: Every measured review system that keeps acceptance fires rarely, and every one that enumerates is overridden between 55% and 98%.
The filter can be a deterministic function of the file, so the projection law holds and no ranking is stored.
The full list one click away means nothing is hidden, which is the difference between suppression and omission.
MHRA already permits an audit trail to be reviewed by exception reporting rather than as a full list, so the compliance reading survives.
questions.flip: If the 40-hunk test shows strangers finishing an exhaustive list without reaching accept-all, enumeration is not the problem and (b) stands.

questions.q: Does clearing a span require a typed reason, and on which acts?
questions.lede: Two evidence lines point opposite ways: alert fatigue says one keystroke, and the compliance buyer wants to know why.

rows.label: Keystrokes per span
cells: one, or a sentence on a revert

rows.label: The sidecar records
cells: who, when, and why on reverts

rows.label: Cost
cells: a text field on the common path
a text field on the rare path

visual.note: No regulation opened requires a reason, or per-span review at all.
visual.caption: Where a typed reason is worth its keystroke.

questions.stakes: A reason field on the common act is the mechanism that made 88.3% of clinical justifications meaningless.
state: The sidecar records reviewed-by and reviewed-at and no reason (`docs/PRODUCT-BRIEF.md:135`).
The drawer offers accept, revert and skip with no text field (`docs/prototype/frontmatter-prototype.html:459`).
Nothing in the plan asks a reviewer to say why.
path: The store was written for a single-person loop, where a reason has no reader.
The paid tier's buyer is the person answerable for a document, and that buyer reads the sidecar rather than writing it.
tension: Of 14,612 overridden clinical alerts, 88.3% of the typed justifications were meaningless.
No regulation opened requires a reason, or per-span review at all; pharma mandates whole-document approval and aviation a per-page revision date.
MHRA permits an audit trail to be reviewed by exception reporting rather than as a full list, which is an argument for reasons on exceptions.
A revert is the only place the product learns what the agent got wrong, and nothing else holds that.

options.label: No reason anywhere — one keystroke clears a span
options.what: The sidecar records who and when, and nothing about why.
gains: The fastest possible act, which the fatigue evidence favours
Nothing to build
costs: A revert records no lesson about the agent
A compliance buyer gets a list of hashes
options.system: No change.
options.screens: No change.

options.label: A reason on rejections and overrides, optional on approvals
options.what: Accepting stays one keystroke; reverting or overriding a refusal asks for a sentence.
gains: Keeps the common path at one keystroke
The rare path carries the only information worth storing
costs: Two acts behave differently, which has to be learnt
A revert becomes slower at the moment of annoyance
options.system: One optional string on the action line.
options.screens: The drawer gains an inline field on revert.

options.label: A reason on every act, stored in the sidecar
options.what: Nothing clears without a typed justification.
gains: The strongest record for a buyer answerable for the document
Uniform behaviour
costs: This is the design that produced 88.3% meaningless reasons
It makes every span a form
options.system: A required string on every line.
options.screens: A field on every act, in the panel and the hover card.

options.label: No reason in MVP-0; add the field when a compliance buyer asks
options.what: Ship the fast path and wait for the five conversations with people who bill for documents.
gains: No design work now
The field is shaped by a real requirement
costs: The pilot's reverts carry no reason to learn from
A later field change rewrites every reader
options.system: No change now, a format change later.
options.screens: No change.

recCase: The cheap act stays one keystroke, so the fatigue evidence is respected on the path taken most often.
A revert is the only place the product learns what the agent got wrong, and it is rare enough to carry a sentence.
Exception reporting is already adjudicated by a regulator, so a compliance reading survives without a field on approvals.
Say plainly in the pitch that no regulation opened requires per-span review, because a compliance buyer punishes the missing caveat.
questions.flip: If the five people who bill for documents say an approval without a stated basis is worthless to them, (c) is the ask.
